t: You are looking at the statue of John Wilkes on Fetter Lane, in the City of London, made by the sculptor James Butler. Wilkes was a radical, journalist and politician, first elected an MP in 1757. In the Middlesex election dispute he fought for the right of voters, rather than the House of Commons, to choose their representatives. In 1771 he helped win printers the right to publish accurate accounts of parliamentary debates. In 1776 he introduced the first bill for parliamentary reform in Parliament.
